regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HER2-positive early breast cancer · before surgery
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: TCHP aims to shrink HER2-positive breast cancer before surgery and reduce the risk of it returning.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected. Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen. Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used. Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: All four medicines are given by infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle, for six cycles before surgery. Surgery findings guide the postoperative treatment. There is no routine take-home chemotherapy pump.
key_points: Six cycles before surgery are one part of the pathway. Surgery findings determine the treatment afterwards; hormone treatment is added only if the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive.
Radiotherapy, endocrine therapy and HER2 continuation can overlap when the MDT considers this appropriate. The map does not prescribe exact postoperative start dates.
The echo interval runs from the HER2 treatment course; changing phase does not reset monitoring.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Triple-negative early breast cancer · before and after surgery
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This pathway combines immunotherapy, chemotherapy and surgery to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early triple-negative breast cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Neoadjuvant → surgery → adjuvant · triple-negative early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops. Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen. Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues. Doxorubicin interferes with enzymes and DNA processes needed for cell division. It can also affect heart muscle, so the team considers previous exposure and cardiac risk. Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycles 1–4: pembrolizumab and carboplatin on Day 1; paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15. Cycles 5–8: pembrolizumab + doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide (AC) on Day 1 every 21 days. Surgery is followed by pembrolizumab when appropriate.
key_points: This is NCCP 00857: four 3-week cycles of carboplatin/weekly paclitaxel with pembrolizumab, then four 3-week AC cycles with pembrolizumab, surgery, and postoperative pembrolizumab when appropriate.
TNBC does not have a routine adjuvant endocrine-therapy lane. Treatment-induced menopause still merits symptom and bone-health assessment.
The interval to surgery and radiation depends on recovery and the MDT plan. Columns show sequence, not equal lengths of time.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer · adjuvant
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: For eligible high-risk node-positive early breast cancer, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence after surgery.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant · high-risk node-positive HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6 proteins. These proteins help cells move towards division. It is combined with endocrine treatment to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early breast cancer. The chosen endocrine medicine either reduces oestrogen production or blocks its action. An aromatase inhibitor may need ovarian suppression before menopause. The exact drug and duration are prescribed separately.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously, with endocrine treatment, for up to two years if appropriate. A 28-day block is shown for orientation; there is no planned tablet-free week. Endocrine treatment usually continues longer.
key_points: Abemaciclib is taken with endocrine treatment after surgery and other indicated local/systemic treatment. Abemaciclib is planned for two years; endocrine treatment commonly continues beyond that.
Entry includes surgery completed, node-positive high-risk criteria and source timing limits. An Oncotype result does not replace these requirements.
The pre-abemaciclib radiation sequence must be agreed explicitly; the NCCP drug schedule does not prescribe an automatic concurrent radiation course.
High risk: ≥4 positive axillary nodes OR 1–3 positive nodes with tumour ≥5 cm or grade 3. Check the source surgery/endocrine timing limits; Oncotype is not a replacement.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Ribociclib with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant aims to control advanced HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer. The exact endocrine partner depends on previous treatment and menopausal status.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic · HR-positive / HER2-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Ribociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6, proteins that help cells move through the cycle of division. Endocrine therapy reduces the hormone signal that can drive HR-positive breast cancer. An aromatase inhibitor (AI) lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant blocks and reduces oestrogen receptors. These are alternative endocrine partners, selected by the team. Ovarian suppression is needed in pre/perimenopausal patients.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Ribociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, followed by seven days off, in a 28-day cycle. The endocrine partner continues according to its own prescription. Treatment continues while it is helping and tolerable.
key_points: Ribociclib is taken for three weeks of each four-week cycle with endocrine treatment. The first two cycles need extra blood checks and an early ECG; cancer-response reviews continue over the longer term.

NCCP v6 and the current manufacturer QT table differ on restart after the first >480–500 ms event in metastatic disease. Interrupt and reconcile with pharmacy/cardiology before restart; no automatic restart dose is inferred.
NCCP eligibility wording is narrower on page 2 than its indications on page 1. Resolve the intended setting, endocrine partner and ovarian-suppression requirements.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Oral moderate–high category; review QT interactions before antiemetic selection
premedication_and_prophylaxis: The ribociclib break is Days 22–28. Your endocrine partner usually continues.
Early blood tests and a Day-14 ECG are important even if you feel well.
patient_education: The ribociclib break is Days 22–28. Your endocrine partner usually continues.
Early blood tests and a Day-14 ECG are important even if you feel well.
Avoid grapefruit; check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements for interactions.
Do not take an extra dose. Take the next prescribed dose at the usual time and contact the team if uncertain.
special_support: Discuss fertility, menopause, sexual health, psychological support, rehabilitation and practical needs.

baseline: ECG; correct low potassium, magnesium, calcium or phosphate
before_each_cycle: ECG: an electrical heart tracing: Before starting and around Day 14 of cycle 1; then as indicated. Starting QTcF must be <450 ms. This is ECG monitoring, not a routine 3-monthly echo programme. Review QT-prolonging/CYP3A medicines and electrolyte abnormalities.

Bloods and electrolytes: Bloods every 2 weeks for cycles 1–2; before cycles 3–6; then as indicated. Electrolytes before each of the first six cycles, then as indicated; intensify monitoring with abnormal results.
Cancer-response imaging: Usually every 2–4 months, adapted to the clinical picture.
Markers, if selected: Alongside the individual response plan.

Bone health with endocrine therapy: At AI/OFS initiation and then by risk. Repeat DEXA is based on baseline bone density, fracture risk and bone treatment. A 12–24-month reassessment can be appropriate near a treatment threshold or when risk changes; it is not an automatic annual scan for everyone.
Week off ribociclib: Days 22–28 of each cycle. This metastatic schedule starts at 600 mg/day unless adjusted. Do not substitute the separate 400 mg/3-year adjuvant ribociclib pathway.
priority_toxicities: Rare serious lung or skin reactions
Hot flushes, joint pain and fatigue
Bone loss with AI / ovarian suppression
urgent_review_signals: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, jaundice, a painful swollen leg or a severe rash promptly. You do not need to identify which medicine caused the symptom.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Ribociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, followed by seven days off, in a 28-day cycle. The endocrine partner continues according to its own prescription. Treatment continues while it is helping and tolerable.
route_and_duration: Ribociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, followed by seven days off, in a 28-day cycle. The endocrine partner continues according to its own prescription. Treatment continues while it is helping and tolerable.
practical_workflow: Confirm the exact tablet strength, endocrine partner, blood-test and ECG plan where relevant.
Take tablets whole at the prescribed times. Abemaciclib is continuous twice daily; ribociclib has a planned 7-day break. Follow the schedule for this card only.
Do not double up or take a replacement dose. Follow the medicine instructions and ask the oncology pharmacist if uncertain.
Confirm symptoms and required test results have been reviewed. Ask whether the prescription changes; do not restart a held medicine yourself.
observation_and_access: Check all new medicines and supplements with oncology/pharmacy, avoid grapefruit, store as labelled and keep away from children. Return unwanted tablets to the pharmacy.

An aromatase inhibitor is generally a daily tablet. Fulvestrant, when selected for metastatic treatment, has loading injections on Days 1, 15 and 29 then monthly. Ovarian-suppression injections have their own prescription and visit schedule.
The CDK4/6 medicine is taken orally. An implanted port or infusion pump is not required for these tablets; other treatment may have separate access needs.

evidence_records.trial_population: A phase III trial of high-risk, node-positive HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer compared two years of abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy with endocrine therapy alone.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: See primary report; the displayed endpoint is explicitly labelled
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Seven-year invasive disease-free survival was 77.4% versus 70.9% (6.5 percentage points difference). This composite endpoint is not the same as overall survival and does not predict an individual outcome. The 2025 primary overall-survival report also found an overall-survival benefit. Treatment eligibility still requires the NCCP high-risk and timing criteria.
